jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Director of Finance provides strategic leadership and overall direction for the finance department at Lopes Limited. As a key partner to the President, Vice-President and senior leadership team, the Director translates business priorities into financial plans, provides clear advice on financial performance and risk, and supports decisions that strengthen profitability, cash flow and long-term growth.
Reporting to the President, the Director is accountable for the quality, integrity and timeliness of financial reporting and for the effectiveness of accounting operations, financial controls and forecasting. The role leads and develops the finance team, establishes clear accountabilities and ensures financial information supports practical decisions across construction, fabrication and project operations.
The primary focus is Lopes Limited. When requested by ownership or senior leadership, the Director also provides financial guidance to sister companies, working with their management teams and finance personnel to strengthen planning, reporting and financial practices within the scope assigned.

What we offer as an employer

Competitive salary
Comprehensive benefits including dental, vision, disability, and life insurance
Company RRSP’s
Wellness and employee assistance programs
Opportunities to grow within your community
Company events
Work-life balance
Free Golf Membership
On-site medical clinic
On-site service center for vehicle repairs at discounted rates
A culture that is built on respect, health, safety, and integrity

Responsibilities

Strategic Financial Leadership:
Lead Lopes Limited’s financial strategy, advise senior leadership, evaluate investments and growth opportunities, and guide commercial decisions to strengthen profitability and financial resilience.
Forecasting and Performance:
Lead forecasting and financial reporting, while coaching department leaders to manage spend, understand results, and take corrective action
Financial Reporting and Project Profitability:
Manage financial closing, reporting, project & departmental costing, and external accountant coordination to ensure accurate financial statements, reliable performance analysis, and sound accounting practices.
Cash Flow Financing and Capital Planning:
Oversee cash flow, working capital, financing, banking relationships, including financial oversight of bonding, insurance and funding opportunities.
Financial Controls Compliance and Risk:
Direct financial policies, internal controls, risk management, tax compliance, secure records and intercompany accounting to ensure accurate reporting and financial accountability.
Finance Department Leadership:
Lead and develop the finance team, oversee accounting and payroll, support workforce and compensation planning, and improve financial systems, processes and coordination across departments.

Qualifications and Experience

Post-secondary education in accounting or business with a CPA designation or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Eight to ten years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership of a finance team and responsibility for financial planning, reporting, and controls
Experience in construction, fabrication, industrial services, or other project-based business, with a strong understanding of job costing, work in progress, and revenue recognition.
Demonstrated ability to advise senior leadership, develop financial strategy, and translate complex information into clear recommendations.
Strong experience in forecasting and cash flow management.
Knowledge of Canadian accounting and tax requirements, with the judgement to engage specialized advisors when needed.
Experience managing relationships with external accountants, and other financial partners; exposure to multiple related companies is an asset.
Advanced Excel and financial systems skills, including the ability to improve reporting and use data to support decisions.
Proven people leadership, sound business judgement, and the ability to challenge assumptions respectfully while building productive working relationships.
High standards of integrity, accuracy, and confidentiality, with the ability to balance strategic priorities and operational deadlines.

We thank all candidates for their interest but only those considered for an interview will be contacted.

At Lopes Limited we are committed to being an equal opportunity employer. We offer a barrier free experience to applicants with accessibility needs. Requests for accommodation can be made at any stage during the recruitment process. Please contact us directly for such arrangements at jobs@lopes.ca

Salary Range: $90,000 - $150,000

jobs.title: Associate Director Finance
jobs.description:
An established, respected national organization is seeking an experienced Associate Director, Finance to provide leadership across financial reporting, investment accounting, budgeting, forecasting and financial controls.
An excellent opportunity for a hands-on finance leader to contribute to a complex, multi-entity environment, strengthen financial reporting practices and support organizational decision-making
Reporting to the senior finance leadership team, this role will oversee core accounting and reporting functions across multiple entities, ensuring financial integrity, regulatory compliance and effective financial stewardship.
Prepare pension financial statements ,
management reports, regulatory filings, and supporting audit documentation in accordance with applicable accounting standards and pension legislation.
Oversee financial reporting, general ledger integrity, consolidations and month-end/year-end close.
Lead budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and variance reporting.
Manage external audit coordination, regulatory filings and compliance requirements.
Strengthen internal controls, accounting policies, processes and financial systems.
Provide technical accounting guidance and business partnership to senior leadership and stakeholders.
Lead, mentor and develop the accounting team.

Qualifications & Experience
CPA designation required.
PENSION ACCOUNTING A MUST

5–8 years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including 3+ years in a leadership role.
Strong experience with multi-entity financial reporting and consolidations.
Knowledge of not-for-profit accounting standards and pension plan financial reporting is required to be considered.
Investment accounting experience is highly desirable.
Strong technical accounting, analytical, communication and leadership skills.

jobs.title: Senior Director Finance
jobs.description:
Senior Director, Finance – The Mustard Seed

This executive search is conducted by Nelson/Kraft & Associates on behalf of The Mustard Seed

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Mustard Seed is searching for a seasoned and collaborative financial leader with initiative and drive to join their team as Senior Director, Finance.
The Senior Director, Finance is the CFO’s principal operational finance leader and trusted second-in-command. The role provides enterprise leadership across accounting, financial reporting, grants, budgeting and forecasting, treasury, audit, internal controls, finance systems, and process improvement. The successful candidate combines deep Controller-level technical expertise with strong people leadership, sound judgment, and the ability to translate financial complexity into practical decisions that support The Mustard Seed’s mission and long-term sustainability.
If you are an experienced CPA and team leader who comes from a mid to large sized organization with similarly complex moving parts, we would love to hear from you!

WHO WE ARE

The Mustard Seed is a Christian humanitarian organization whose vision is to build community, grow hope, and support change. Intentionally following Jesus Christ and partnering with the community, The Mustard Seed combats the root causes of poverty in Alberta, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan and works to create positive, lasting change in the lives of those we serve. The Mustard Seed provides basic services (food, clothing, housing, and support services), education, and employment to those living in poverty in the locations we serve.

OUR HISTORY

Pat Nixon founded The Mustard Seed in 1984 with a single street ministry location in central Calgary. Today, the organization operates in multiple cities – Calgary, Edmonton, Red Deer, Medicine Hat, and Grande Prairie in Alberta, Kamloops in British Columbia, and Saskatoon in Saskatchewan. All locations offer a different range of programs and services to serve our most vulnerable community members.

Programs & Services Include:

Basic Needs – emergency shelter, meals, clothing and hygiene items
Health and Wellness
Housing
Employment
Spiritual Care
Community Engagement
Community Impact Centres

IDEAL CANDIDATE PROFILE

The ideal candidate is a senior CPA finance leader with deep Controller-level technical expertise and a successful record of leading finance functions in a complex, larger organization. They have personally led significant year-end audits, overseen accounting and financial reporting, managed grant-funded operations, strengthened internal controls, improved budgeting and forecasting, and led finance systems and process transformation. They are equally comfortable resolving a technical accounting issue, guiding a manager, challenging a budget assumption, working with auditors and funders, and advising the CFO and Executive Team. The successful candidate will provide dependable operational leadership while helping modernize Finance and strengthen The Mustard Seed’s financial sustainability, stewardship, and organizational capacity.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Professional Designations, Required

Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing.
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, commerce, business administration, or a related discipline.
Ongoing professional development in accounting standards, financial reporting, governance, internal controls, audit, risk management, and finance leadership.

Preferred Assets

CRMA, CFE, CIA, or another relevant risk, controls, audit, fraud, or governance designation.
Advanced training or certification in ERP systems, data analytics, business intelligence, financial systems implementation, finance transformation, or project management.

Experience Requirements

Approximately 12 to 15+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including significant senior leadership responsibility.
A minimum of 5 to 7 years of leading managers and professional finance teams in a large or larger mid-sized, complex organization.
Significant experience serving in a Controller, Corporate Controller, or equivalent senior controllership role, with accountability for the integrity of financial reporting, accounting operations, internal controls, and close processes.
Extensive experience leading the annual external audit from planning through completion, including audit schedules, working papers, issue resolution, management responses, and relationships with external auditors and governance committees.
Demonstrated leadership across financial reporting, general accounting, grants accounting, budgeting and forecasting, treasury, internal controls, risk management, and audit coordination.
Substantial experience with grant-funded operations, including grant budgeting, restricted funding, contribution agreements, eligible expenditures, cost allocations, claims, financial reporting, compliance, funder audits, and closeout.
Experience leading finance systems and process improvement, including ERP optimization or implementation, systems integration, reporting automation, data quality, business intelligence, and finance workflow redesign.
Experience building, restructuring, developing, or stabilizing a finance function while maintaining reliable day-to-day delivery.
Experience advising executives and presenting clear, decision-focused financial information to senior leadership and governance bodies.

Strongly Preferred

Experience in a large charity, not-for-profit, healthcare, public sector, social services, affordable housing, or similarly complex mission-driven environment.
Experience managing a large portfolio of municipal, provincial, federal, or other government funding agreements.
Deep practical experience with fund accounting, restricted contributions, contribution revenue recognition, capital projects, and government-funded initiatives.
Experience with Salesforce-based ERP environments such as Certinia/FinancialForce, budgeting and forecasting tools, Tableau or similar BI platforms, and broader data governance initiatives.

Location:
Calgary, AB
Application Deadline:
November 27, 2026
Start Date:
TBD
Salary Range
: $125,000-$130,000

ABOUT US

Nelson/Kraft & Associates Inc. is an executive consulting firm that specializes in working with not-for-profits and for-profit businesses across Canada, assisting them in the placement of senior executives and directors.
Nelson/Kraft & Associates Inc. welcomes and encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position. Nelson/Kraft & Associates Inc. is committed to the principles of diversity and inclusion in its hiring practices, and will only make distinctions among interested applicants in accordance with the applicable Human Rights legislation.
Nelson/Kraft & Associates Inc. also welcomes and encourages applications from candidates with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in the selection process. If you require disability-related accommodation during the recruitment process, please contact us.
